## Submission Rules (Sessionize 2026 verified; 2027 UNVERIFIED)

GopherCon-specific rules from Guidelines for Proposals, excluding Recommended Reading (verified 2026-10-17: <https://sessionize.com/gophercon-2026/>). 2027 reuse is UNVERIFIED:

- No Markdown/formatting shortcuts in Sessionize; untranslated formatting hurts rating.
- Only 25-minute talks; big ideas of general interest to entire attendee base, all experience levels.
- One presenter only; no partner presentations.
- No Q&A time in allotment.
- All presentations recorded, published on Gopher Academy YouTube after conference.
- Content must relate to Go or removed from review.
- Talk outline with approximate timing per section required; thoughtful outlines favored.
- Double-blind review; no PII or identity-disclosing links. At discretion, disqualified or asked to fix. OSS library link allowed unless de-anonymizing; then state it can be provided if shortlisted.
- Mentoring available pre-submission and for speaking accommodations: `info@gopheracademy.com`.
- Speaker support: hotel/travel assistance if company does not cover; unused portion donated to scholarship fund. All speakers get one general admission ticket.
- Diverse voices; first-time, neurodivergent, new members encouraged; equal-quality tie-break to diverse/new content; some invited slots outside CFP.

## Submission Fields (historical shape, 2027 UNVERIFIED)

Historical shape from Gopher Academy era; live 2027 field names, limits, voice, selectors vs free text are all UNVERIFIED:

- Title: short, pithy, can be punny/cryptic; avoid BuzzFeed/clickbait ("seatbait"). Cute vague titles punished — attendees pick talks minutes before start. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/gophercon-2017/writing-a-successful-gophercon-proposal/> , <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/> , <https://carolynvanslyck.com/blog/2018/12/talk-at-gophercon/>)
- Abstract: historical limit 300 characters; hook + elevator pitch; one sentence topic + one sentence takeaway; state topic and target audience; no teasing. Used on website/agenda. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/> , <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/gophercon-2017/writing-a-successful-gophercon-proposal/>)
- Description: long-form; historical floor 200-300 words minimum; thin proposals "rarely chosen over detailed ones". Shape: intro paragraph(s) + outline + conclusion paragraph(s), ideally the actual talk intro/conclusion. Must cover: core topic, target audience, Go-community relevance + "why now", impact/takeaways, why you (experience, not expertise). (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/> , <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/gophercon-2017/writing-a-successful-gophercon-proposal/> , <https://dave.cheney.net/2017/02/12/how-to-write-a-successful-conference-proposal>)
- Outline: required, with timing per section (ranges + skippable/expandable sections to prove time control). Rule of thumb: 25-min = 1 topic + 1 subtopic; 45-min = 2-3 topics, 1-2 subtopics. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/> , <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-advice/>)
- Reviewer-only notes: historical advice to disclose fully is superseded by 2026 no-PII rule; do not include identifying links. Reviewers score blind on title/abstract/description only. (historical verified: <https://carolynvanslyck.com/blog/2018/12/talk-at-gophercon/> , <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/gophercon-2017/writing-a-successful-gophercon-proposal/>; superseded 2026-10-17: <https://sessionize.com/gophercon-2026/>)
- Voice (abstract/description person): UNVERIFIED for live CFP. Do not assume third person.
- Selectors vs free text: UNVERIFIED for live CFP.
- Bio: human-owned. Agents never touch it. Customize per talk to highlight relevant background. (verified process: <https://carolynvanslyck.com/blog/2018/12/talk-at-gophercon/>)

## Speaker Constraints on File (2026-10-17; 2027 UNVERIFIED)

- Eligible main-track format for 2026: 25-minute talks only. (verified: <https://sessionize.com/gophercon-2026/>) Historical 45-min/keynotes/tutorials/workshops do not carry to 2027 without live verification.
- 2026 had pre-conference workshops (half/full-day, separate ticket, hands-on) + Main Theatre Lightning Talks ≤7 minutes, separate June process opened early June closed June 22nd. (verified: <https://gophercon.com/> , <https://www.gophercon.com/agenda>) Whether LT counts as CFP format for this brief is UNVERIFIED.
- Include a concrete timed structure matching the chosen slot; reviewers check achievability (no over/under-run, no rambling). (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/> , <https://dave.cheney.net/2017/02/12/how-to-write-a-successful-conference-proposal>)

## Strictness

Medium-high, story-driven. Odds cited ~10% at review vs ~25% (3 tracks + hallway) at attendance; hundreds of proposals, often 100+ in final 48h. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-storytelling/> , <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-proposal-writing-for-procrastinators/>)

Reviewers reward (GopherCon-specific; Sessionize rules first, recent program evidence second):

- Go relevance that fails substitution test; non-Go topics need explicit why GopherCon / why now. Enforced as removal rule in 2026. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/gophercon-2017/writing-a-successful-gophercon-proposal/> , <https://sessionize.com/gophercon-2026/>)
- Diverse voices; first-time, neurodivergent, new members encouraged; equal-quality tie-break to diverse/new content; some invited slots outside CFP. (verified 2026-10-17: <https://sessionize.com/gophercon-2026/>)
- Experience over expertise; just-in-time learning punished. (verified: <https://carolynvanslyck.com/blog/2018/12/talk-at-gophercon/> , <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/>)
- Story, not reference post; mistakes and what did not go as planned. But 2026 program shows pure explainers/surveys are NOT auto-excluded: sample of 11 main-track/LT entries, 4 story/experience-explicit, 7 explainer/survey (e.g. Go Generics deep-dive, Self-Optimizing Worker Pools, Inside Out 3-layer observability compare, (Sync)testing constraints). Accepted explainers carry mental model/framework/practical examples with aggregated takeaways. (verified 2026-10-17: <https://www.gophercon.com/agenda> , <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/>)
- Proposal as newspaper, talk as book; no buried lede. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-storytelling/>)
- Tight focus 1-2 takeaways as rule of thumb with stated exceptions ("may not be applicable to all types of talks"); novelty preferred. 2026 sample shows 3-element structures are common. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/> , <https://www.gophercon.com/agenda>)
- First-hand insight over docs rehash; no sales pitch. (verified: <https://medium.com/@fox/how-to-write-a-successful-conference-proposal-4461509d3e32>)
- Early submit / mentoring contact before deadline. 2017 pre-deadline feedback evolved to 2026 email mentoring. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/gophercon-2017/writing-a-successful-gophercon-proposal/> , <https://sessionize.com/gophercon-2026/>)

Reviewers punish:

- Rule violations (~30% sample), sloppy formatting/typos, ableist/shaming language. 2026 adds Markdown-submission penalty. (verified: <https://medium.com/@fox/how-to-write-a-successful-conference-proposal-4461509d3e32> , <https://sessionize.com/gophercon-2026/>)
- Selling Go to Gophers. (verified: <https://dave.cheney.net/2017/02/12/how-to-write-a-successful-conference-proposal>)
- Vague/cute titles, teasing abstracts, detail-free descriptions; PII disclosure risks disqualification in 2026. (verified above + <https://sessionize.com/gophercon-2026/>)
- Static blog/Readme content; sales pitches. (basic knowledge, see below)

General craft (incident-first, linear chain, takeaways) intentionally excluded — belongs in agent definitions.

## Basic Knowledge (cross-conference, weak preference)

Sessionize Recommended Reading treated as baseline, not GopherCon-specific preference. YouTube fetches returned HTTP 401 on 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-17; summaries below are user-provided from `memo.md` (2026-10-17), UNVERIFIED against video:

- Carolyn Van Slyck "Write a Go Conference Proposal" (~1h): usefulness/takeaways over story; Go relevance via substitution test; reviewer-only notes for outline/evidence/links; clear concise titles, avoid jargon/in-jokes; expertise not required, audience benefit first; meetup practice recommended.
- Tom Lyons "Dos and Don'ts" (~4.5min): Dos are clarity, Go-specificity, concrete detail (outline, code, story), why-you, professional tone, timing; Don'ts are Go-unrelated themes, sales pitches, static blog-sufficient content, sloppy grammar/emoji. Reviewers want education, stimulation, new ideas.

Full reading list (verified 2026-10-17: <https://sessionize.com/gophercon-2026/>): Brandow Storytelling on Stage series, Cheney guide, Lyons video, Olsen guide, Szczur guide, Van Slyck blog + video.
